observations: Single photo shows a greasy, disassembled automatic transmission/gearbox unit with a blue torque-converter cover visible.
No VIN plate, parts tag, sticker, or stamped pin-count/model number is visible or legible anywhere in the photo.
A watermark reading 'AUTO SPARE PARTS' is overlaid on the image; this is a shop/seller watermark, not proof of origin.
Casing shows oil residue and surface grime consistent with a used part, but no internal view, no bench/test rig, and no video of it turning is shown.

claims.evidence: No plate, tag, or pin-count visible in photo 0 to confirm make, model, year range, or pin count.
Subjective seller language, no supporting evidence possible from a photo.
No import sticker, customs tag, or paperwork shown.
No video or bench-test clip showing the gearbox running or shifting.
No odometer, donor-vehicle documentation, or mileage tag shown.
No clear shot of bolt heads/seals to confirm casing has not been previously opened.

risks.risk: Wrong fitment/model entirely (gearbox may not actually be a 22-pin Camry unit for the stated years)
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped parts ID plate or pin-count on the connector showing matching code.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unidentified/unverified-fitment used gearbox, not as a confirmed Camry unit

risks.risk: Internal damage or non-functioning unit despite 'tested' claim
risks.proof: Video clip of the gearbox being bench-tested or installed and shifting through gears.

risks.risk: High mileage or prior rebuild/opening hidden by cleaning
risks.proof: Photo of donor vehicle's odometer/import tag, or close-up of casing bolts for tamper signs.
risks.if_unproven: priced as high-mileage/opened, i.e. lowest condition tier

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the parts ID plate / stamped pin-count on the connector that confirms model and year fitment.
A video of the gearbox being tested on a bench or in a vehicle, showing it shift through gears without noise.
Photo of import/customs documentation or Belgium shipping paperwork to support the Tokunbo claim.
response.reason: The single photo shows only a generic, unlabeled used gearbox with no visible plate, tag, or pin-count to confirm it is the specific Toyota Camry 22-pin unit claimed, and fitment is the main price driver across the comparables (ranging from budget gearboxes to premium ones); without that identifying shot even a worst-case price cannot be fixed.
